correctness.rationale: The exact five-map cosine product follows from independent digits. Primitive residues mod 3 give only axis candidates; mod 9 restricts them to signed sizes 1 and 2. For any later departure from either 3-adic branch, the offending cosine is strictly negative because \(3^j>6a\) for \(j\ge3\) and \(a\le2\); the factor falls below 3/5 and the full product below 6/25. The explicit rational inequality \(B>(58/225)(77/81)>6/25\) certifies both surviving classes, and monotonicity of cosine establishes A>B. The checker replays 58349 supplementary assertions. Finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The uniform cross Vicsek measure is a canonical singular planar self-similar probability measure. The first two lattice Fourier moduli and infinite extremizing families are natural precise invariants for its torus convolution operator, and the explicit separation of every other Fourier mode below 6/25 gives a motivated spectral decomposition. Neither the product mask nor numerical correctness alone supplies this frequency rigidity. The third-band threshold is deliberately not claimed optimal.
